rationale: Both independently catch the same high-value, not-in-ground-truth bug (seed_tts_eval double-resampling of already-24kHz audio) with near-identical, well-grounded reasoning. X covers all three real GT threads (audio_vae config mutation, dropped language/dialect field, patch_emission +2) with depth that mirrors how they actually got resolved (hedging 'if intentional, document; else fix'), while Y's treatment of the language-removal and +2 threads is thin, tacked onto a truncated 'additional observations' appendix. X loses precision points for a suspicious, likely-inaccurate 'verified locally' claim that the encoder is actually truncated (the real PR thread confirms only stale config metadata, no behavioral change) and unverifiable merge-SHA narrative; Y is more consistently evidence-cited and technically accurate but padded with redundant near-duplicate 'validated' entries and less scannable, evidence-dump formatting. X's clearer severity tiers and concrete suggested diffs make it more actionable overall.
